item.title: Low-cost non-iterative Sylvester solvers for dynamical low-rank approximation of reaction-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop low-cost non-iterative Sylvester solvers for dynamical low-rank approximation of reaction-diffusion equations and incorporate them into a basis-update \& Galerkin mass-lumped finite element method (\mbox{BUG-MLFEM}). By incorporating mass lumping via Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, the spatial discretization yields a matrix differential equation equipped with diagonal positive-definite mass matrices. We establish the weighted dynamical low-rank approximation (WDLRA) within the Galerkin framework of the MLFEM system, proving the theoretical equivalence between the BUG integrator and MLFEM on low-rank subspaces, which guarantees the discrete well-posedness of the implicit BUG steps. To overcome the severe computational bottleneck of standard $O(m^3+n^3)$ Sylvester solvers, we develop tailored, low-cost non-iterative solvers that exploit the inherent sparse-by-small algebraic structure. Under Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions (BCs), the large coefficient matrices are banded, enabling efficient diagonalization of the small $r \times r$ factor matrix and reducing the per-step computational complexity to $O((m+n)r^2)$ and storage to $O((m+n)r)$. For periodic BCs, we combine this diagonalization strategy with a rank-2 Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury update to handle wrap-around corner entries at negligible additional cost. Numerical experiments demonstrate first-order temporal and $(k+1)$th-order spatial convergence of the proposed BUG-MLFEM in the discrete $L^2$ norm, where $k$ denotes the polynomial degree of the finite element space, together with significant computational speedups over existing low-rank integrators.
item.dc:creator: Joy Saha, Jun Yang, Peimeng Yin

item.title: Two-level additive Schwarz preconditioners with GDSW coarse spaces for high-order discretizations in 2D
item.description: arXiv:2610.18502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners with Generalized Dryja-Smith-Widlund (GDSW) and Reduced GDSW (RGDSW) coarse spaces for high-order finite element methods (FEM) and virtual element methods (VEM) are investigated and applied to the Poisson problem in 2D. The GDSW coarse space is a well-established robust choice for preconditioners in domain decomposition, while the RGDSW coarse space offers a competitive alternative by reducing the coarse problem dimension while maintaining robustness. On the theoretical side, a condition number bound for both preconditioners is proved for conforming $\mathbb{P}_k$ and $\mathbb{Q}_k$ finite element spaces with explicit dependence on the polynomial degree $k$. Through numerical experiments on structured triangular and quadrilateral meshes for FEM and on polygonal meshes for VEM, it is demonstrated that both GDSW and RGDSW maintain scalability properties across polynomial orders up to $k=9$ for selected degrees. The RGDSW approach achieves a reduction in the coarse problem dimension by a factor of approximately three compared to GDSW while maintaining competitive iteration counts.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Bevilacqua, Axel Klawonn, Martin Lanser, Adam Wasiak

item.title: A two-level preconditioner for discontinuous virtual element methods with irregular subdomains
item.description: arXiv:2610.18580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and analyze a two-level overlapping additive Schwarz preconditioner for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of virtual element spaces on general polygonal meshes in two dimensions, for a second-order elliptic problem whose coefficient is constant on each subdomain and may have large jumps across the interface. The discretization is a weighted symmetric interior penalty formulation: the averages carry the coefficient and the penalty is scaled by its harmonic mean across each edge, which keeps the method consistent and makes the constants of the analysis independent of the coefficient. The coarse space is obtained from a virtual, continuous partition of unity with a single degree of freedom per subdomain vertex, and is therefore applicable to the irregular subdomains produced by a graph partitioner; the discrete harmonic extension used to build it may be replaced by a cheaper projection onto polynomials of low degree. We prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $C(1+\log(H/h))(1+H/\delta)$, where $H$, $h$ and $\delta$ denote the subdomain diameter, the mesh size and the overlap, and where $C$ is independent of the number of subdomains and of the contrast of the coefficient, provided the latter is quasi-monotone. This is the same bound known for the conforming case and the analysis allows for hanging nodes. We also show, by an explicit example, that the quasi-monotonicity assumption cannot be dispensed with. Numerical experiments with structured triangular, hexagonal and Voronoi meshes, and with subdomains obtained both by uniform partitioning and by METIS, confirm the theory.
item.dc:creator: Juan G. Calvo, C\'esar Herrera

item.title: Fully discrete multi-entropy-stable compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.18837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop fully discrete multi-entropy-stable high-order compact Runge--Kutta discontinuous Galerkin (cRKDG) methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. Our main result is a weak cell entropy inequality for multi-dimensional systems after one full high-order Runge--Kutta (RK) time step. The proof exploits the cell-local intermediate stages of cRKDG: their perturbations are controlled by the initial in-cell variation. The analysis does not require a strong stability preserving decomposition or stagewise entropy correction. For a sufficiently dissipative Lax--Friedrichs flux and explicit RK methods with nonnegative output weights, the inequality holds under a suitable time-step restriction for strongly convex entropy pairs. For a prescribed, uniformly conditioned family of such entropies, common dissipation and time-step conditions ensure weak cell entropy stability for all entropy pairs. A single cell-average-preserving scaling at the end of each step then enforces all corresponding strong cell entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also prove a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem: under the stated assumptions, any strongly convergent sequence of numerical solutions converges to a weak solution satisfying all prescribed entropy inequalities. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions demonstrate high-order accuracy, the benefit of multiple entropy constraints for nonconvex scalar problems, and robust performance on shock problems.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Sun

item.title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.
item.dc:creator: Kenshiro Oguri

item.title: Generalized PINN-Based Inverse Estimation of Spatially Varying Heat Transfer Coefficients with Transfer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study investigates generalized boundary representations and transfer learning for physics-informed neural-network (PINN) estimation of spatially varying convective heat transfer coefficients (HTCs) in jet impingement cooling. Piecewise-linear (PWL) and neural-network boundary estimators are inferred from transient interior-temperature measurements and evaluated against CFD-CHT reference HTC profiles at Reynolds numbers of 5000, 10000 and 15000. A discrete Adjoint-FEM formulation with gradient regularization based on the $H^1$-seminorm provides an independent inverse-method comparison. Transfer learning is investigated under two source-target conditions: transfer between noise levels at the same Reynolds number, and transfer from a controlled Gaussian-profile problem to CFD-CHT-derived target problems at different Reynolds numbers. For the representative Re = 5000 target with 5% measurement noise, quadratic, PWL, and neural-network PINNs achieve relative HTC-profile errors of 5.08, 5.31 and 5.19%, respectively, while generalized representations reduce the error for the Re = 15000 target from 16.76% for the quadratic PINN to 14.41% and 14.46%. Transfer learning reduces target-training time by 57.86-81.71% for fixed-Reynolds-number transfer and by 50.59-84.94% for Gaussian-to-CHT transfer. Its effect on reconstruction accuracy is target dependent: fixed-profile PWL transfer remains within 0.30 percentage points of scratch training, whereas Gaussian-to-CHT transfer produces differences of 0.10-1.52 percentage points across targets and representations. These results demonstrate that generalized PINN representations can accommodate spatially varying HTC profiles without a prescribed quadratic form, while transfer learning can substantially reduce target-training cost for repeated inverse estimation, with the resulting reconstruction accuracy depending on source-target compatibility.
item.dc:creator: Pradipan Maitra, Jariful Hassan, Arijit Hazra

item.title: A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.14764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Leplat, Zeyu Dong, Junfeng Yin

item.title: A quantum algorithm for meshless lattice Boltzmann method with unitary interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a mass-weighted meshless formulation for the shifted incompressible lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) whose streaming step is exactly unitary, combining with the Carleman embedding. In traditional meshless LBM, on a scattered node set the semi-Lagrangian streaming step is an interpolation, which is not unitary; a generic block encoding of this matrix therefore requires a normalization proportional to its sparsity and logarithmically many ancillas. To overcome the non-unitarity, we instead express the interpolation as the exponential exp(a Dx + b Dy) of mimetic derivative operators. Endowing each node with its Voronoi mass and applying a mass-weighted similarity transform renders these derivative operators skew-Hermitian by enforcing moment constraints together with low-wave number trigonometric differentiation conditions, so that the interpolation becomes exactly unitary. Such unitarization of interpolation leave the local collision step unchanged up to a rescaling of its quadratic term, where the same weights define the amplitude encoding of the distribution functions. For quasi-uniform node sets, the mass-weighting diagonal remains within a unit-order normalization that degrades only mildly as the Carleman truncation order grows, thereby mitigating the cost of block encoding. Numerical experiments on the Taylor Green vortex confirm that the method reproduces the full meshless LBM, with the velocity error decreasing as the Carleman order increases.
item.dc:creator: Chi Zhang, Hefeng Wang, Hua Xiang

item.title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Zeroth-Order Stochastic Bilevel Optimization with Inexact Lower Level Solves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15047v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Variational regularization techniques are dominant in the field of mathematical imaging. The expressiveness of these methods heavily depends on the adopted regularization formulation which usually involves a number of parameters which have to be fine-tuned by the user. To circumvent the heavy computational costs associated with this parameter tuning, data-driven learning strategies have turned out to be a useful strategy. Selecting parameters by learning from data gives rise to a hierarchical (bilevel) optimization problem, which is in general computationally hard to solve. Our aim in this paper is to develop a data-efficient solution strategy for the bilevel learning problem. To that end, we propose a multilevel Monte Carlo derivative-free optimization method that couples Gaussian smoothing of the upper-level objective (parameter selection) with a hierarchy of lower-level (variational regularization) solution accuracies. Being agnostic towards the specific way the lower-level problem is solved, we derive explicit oracle complexity and computational cost statements for approximately solving the entire bilevel learning problem. Our statements are parameterized by the employed lower-level solution method, thus allowing for a direct cost accounting from the variational reconstruction method to the parameter selection problem. This enables us to give a universal end-to-end complexity analysis of bilevel learning, valid for the most important optimization routines in inverse problems, rather than for a specific choice of methods.
item.dc:creator: Neil K. Chada, Mohammad S. Salehi, Mathias Staudigl, Simon Weissmann

item.title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.
item.dc:creator: Abdelhafid Zenati, Kamal Youcef-Toumi

item.title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.15573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Liao, Xiucheng Li

item.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.
item.dc:creator: Comlan Edmond Koudjinan

item.title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
item.description: arXiv:2610.16148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break. In the resulting scheme, the ghost values are interpolated bilinearly at the image point; solid and dry nodes are excluded, and the weights of the remaining nodes are renormalized. Mass is conserved by solving the continuity equation in cut-cell form, while the momentum equations are left unchanged. The proposed scheme is about as accurate as the ghost-cell method without this modification and preserves a lake at rest whose shoreline crosses an immersed wall. Because only the continuity equation is modified, it avoids the treatment of the momentum equations on cut cells (wall pressure, cell merging) that a full cut-cell method requires.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Yaegashi (Independent Researcher)

item.title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.16249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincar\'e disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Angino, Tam\'as D\'ozsa, Matthias Voigt

item.title: Preconditioned Latent Variable Proximal Point Method for Optimal Control Problems with Control Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.16678v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The latent variable proximal point (LVPP) method solves optimization problems in function spaces with pointwise constraints by a sequence of smooth subproblems whose iterates are strictly feasible. We apply it to linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problems. Control and observation are distributed but may be restricted to subdomains. We prove that the LVPP subproblems are well posed in appropriate function spaces, that the iteration converges for every sequence of proximity parameters with divergent sum, and that it delivers the Lagrange multiplier of the constraint as a by-product. We interpret the Newton step for the LVPP subproblem as a linear-quadratic optimal control problem with a spatially varying control cost, and we show that Newton's method converges locally quadratically. The Newton systems are solved by the minimal residual method with a block-diagonal preconditioner. We prove that the spectrum of the Newton operator with respect to the inner product defined by the preconditioner is bounded independently of the proximity parameter, the iterate, the mesh and the observation and control domains. The results are combined into a complete algorithm, and tested in numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Nico Haaf, Roland Herzog

item.title: A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.17026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the boundary corrector $\theta_\epsilon$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of G\'{e}rard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $\theta_\epsilon$ converges to the solution $\theta^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of G\'{e}rard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. This equation is a Riccati equation in which the derivative in depth is replaced by a commutator with the derivative along $n$. This cell problem can therefore be solved by a Riccati doubling algorithm, and we can compute $d(n)$ at irrational normals without rational approximation. Dropping the commutator term in the cell equation gives an operator square root approximation for $N_n$ that captures the leading term of $d(n)$ for small contrast, for the truncated problem. Finally, we approximate $\theta_\epsilon$ at finite $\epsilon$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $\theta^*$, and test it on the disk.
item.dc:creator: Shari Moskow

item.title: Failure Modes of Interior-Point SDP Solvers on Moment--SOS Hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2610.17261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard semidefinite programming (SDP) solvers working in double precision can become unreliable on difficult problems, even when their output appears plausible. We study this issue for SDP problems arising from high-order moment-SOS hierarchies. Three polynomial optimization problems are analysed by comparing standard double-precision computations with reference solutions obtained using the extended-precision solver \mbox{Loraine\,64x4}. We observe two distinct patterns of numerical failure. In \emph{false convergence}, the computed bounds form a smooth sequence but approach the limit at the wrong rate. In \emph{stagnation}, the sequence develops a plateau or oscillations and no longer reflects the convergence of the underlying hierarchy. We introduce an empirical effective condition number based on the positive spectral components of the primal and dual solution matrices. It serves as a warning indicator rather than an error bound, and its growth accompanies numerical deterioration in our examples. We also examine the imbalance between primal and dual spectral conditioning and a Cholesky inverse residuum as potential diagnostic indicators. The results show that solver termination messages and apparently regular convergence curves may be insufficient to establish the reliability of high-order moment-SOS bounds.
item.dc:creator: Michal Kocvara

item.title: Beyond periodicity: Fourier methods for optimal control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fourier-based spectral methods provide compact global approximations, permit simple differentiation and integration, and achieve spectral convergence for smooth periodic functions. Their use in finite-horizon optimal control problems (OCPs) is nevertheless challenged by the generally nonperiodic state and control trajectories: endpoint mismatch induces artificial discontinuities and can destroy spectral convergence. Leveraging Eckhoff-type endpoint-correction techniques, we develop a Fourier-based spectral framework for OCPs with possibly nonlinear dynamics and constraints. The correction improves convergence without enlarging the set of decision variables, yielding an efficient finite-dimensional numerical method. Furthermore, we formulate selected dynamics and obstacle-avoidance constraints through Sobolev residual bounds, which incorporate information about the residuals over the entire time horizon and improve constraint satisfaction. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate competitive computational performance, lower residual errors, and improved solution accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Milena Ispiryan, Vahagn Makaryan, Lusine Poghosyan, Tigran Bakaryan

item.title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.
item.dc:creator: Solomon Quinn, Charles L. Epstein

item.title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
item.description: arXiv:2610.18242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Bagagiolo, Andrea Corli, Stefan Moreti, Massimiliano D. Rosini

item.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with H\"older Continuous Terms
item.description: arXiv:2610.18370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of H\"older continuous functions and satisfies the $\sigma$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $\sigma = 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (\epsilon^{-1}) \epsilon^{2 (\underline{\alpha} - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $\epsilon$-approximate solution, where $\underline{\alpha} \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{\"o}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Chen, C. T. Kelley, Lei Wang

item.title: Orientation Estimation of Cryo-EM Images for Molecules with Arbitrary Symmetry by Semidefinite Programming
item.dc:creator: Yunpeng Shi, Amit Singer, Jinxin Wang, Ruiyi Yang

item.title: Sampling with collective variables: Relative error analysis for umbrella sampling under general conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the expectation of a function (observable) with respect to a high-dimensional probability distribution, under the assumption that a low-dimensional collective variable map captures all the directions of slow mixing for the distribution. More precisely, under the assumption that the fibers of the collective variable map satisfy a log-Sobolev inequality, we establish non-asymptotic relative-error guarantees for this problem using the eigenvector method for umbrella sampling (EMUS). Our analysis applies to both log-Lipschitz observables and indicator of convex sets, and gives complexity bounds that are polynomial in regularity parameters and inverse relative accuracy, and exponential in the dimension of the collective variable space. As a relative error guarantee, our bounds apply to rare event estimation. We consider Gaussian biasing windows defined on a low-dimensional collective variable space and analyze a modified sparse matrix version of EMUS. The bounds quantify the effect of the map through mixing of the conditional distribution and fluctuation of the observable along the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Holden Lee, Matheau Santana-Gijzen, Jonathan Weare

item.title: Viscosity-uniform error estimates for a semi-implicit Fourier method in Besov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2406.12320v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove error estimates for a semi-implicit Fourier--Galerkin method for two-dimensional incompressible flow on the torus, with viscosity $0\le\nu\le1$. The temporal error is first order in $H^s$ for $H^{s+2}$ initial data and integer $s\ge1$. For data in $B^m_{2,1}$, with integer $m\ge3$, the fully discrete error is of order $\tau+N^{-(m-2)}$ in $B^1_{2,1}$ and $B^0_{\infty,1}$. These estimates hold on a common local interval, with constants and time-step thresholds independent of viscosity and Fourier resolution. For data in $B^{2+\varepsilon}_{2,1}$, $0<\varepsilon<1$, the error relative to Euler flow is bounded by $C(\tau^{(1+\varepsilon)/2}+N^{-\varepsilon} +\nu^{(1+\varepsilon)/2})$. The consistency bounds use viscosity-weighted regularity. Orthogonality of the Leray and Fourier projectors in the block energies gives the endpoint estimates, and stability with respect to the initial data yields the fractional rate. An $L^2$ residual tolerance $\delta$ contributes $CN\delta$ to the endpoint error of computed iterates. We report refinement studies for smooth and fixed multiscale data, together with qualitative flow comparisons. An exactly solvable rough shear has fractional errors, up to logarithms, in $B^1_{2,1}$ and first-order errors in $B^0_{\infty,1}$.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Cheng, Zhaonan Luo, Sheng Wang

item.title: Computational Math with Neural Networks is Hard
item.description: arXiv:2505.17751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish asymptotic complexity barriers for three basic numerical tasks with neural-network data: integration of a network realization, solution of a Poisson problem with a neural-network right-hand side, and multiplication by a neural-network encoded matrix. A common reduction encodes Boolean formulas as ReLU networks and reduces Boolean satisfiability to each task. Any algorithm improving on the resulting convergence-rate bounds would contradict the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH). These bounds hold even with full access to the network representation, including all weights. The core reductions use networks with three hidden layers, width linear in the number of Boolean variables, bounded realizations, and sparse connectivity. A finite-precision Monte Carlo quadrature attains the optimal rate for integration up to logarithmic factors, so the lower bound for integration is sharp. We show slightly weaker lower bounds for networks with two hidden layers and provide fast quadrature algorithms for one-hidden-layer networks.
item.dc:creator: Michael Feischl, Benedikt Gr\"assle, Fabian Zehetgruber

item.title: On efficient multigrid solvers for mixed-degree local discontinuous Galerkin multiphase Stokes problems
item.description: arXiv:2506.09933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We design and investigate efficient multigrid solvers for multiphase Stokes problems discretised via mixed-degree local discontinuous Galerkin methods. Using the template of a standard multigrid V-cycle, we develop a smoother analogous to element-wise block Gauss-Seidel, except the diagonal block inverses are replaced with an approximation that balances the smoothing of the velocity and pressure variables, factoring in the unequal scaling of the various Stokes system operators, and optimised via two-grid local Fourier analysis. We evaluate the performance of the multigrid solver across an extensive range of two- and three-dimensional test problems, including steady-state and unsteady, standard-form and stress-form, single-phase and high-contrast multiphase Stokes problems, with multiple kinds of boundary conditions and various choices of polynomial degree. In the lowest-degree case, i.e., that of piecewise constant pressure fields, we observe reliable multigrid convergence rates, though not especially fast. However, in every other case, we see rapid convergence rates matching those of classical Poisson-style geometric multigrid methods; e.g., 5 iterations reduce the Stokes system residual by 5 to 10 orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Robert I. Saye

item.title: On the Upper Bounds for the Matrix Spectral Norm
item.description: arXiv:2506.15660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the spectral norm of a matrix using only matrix-vector products. We propose a new Counterbalance estimator that provides upper bounds on the norm and derive probabilistic guarantees on its underestimation. Compared to standard approaches such as the power method, the proposed estimator produces significantly tighter upper bounds in both synthetic and real-world settings. Our method is especially effective for matrices with fast-decaying spectra, such as those arising in deep learning and inverse problems.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Naumov, Maxim Rakhuba, Denis Ryapolov, Sergey Samsonov

item.title: Dimension of Bi-degree $(d,d)$ Spline Spaces with the Highest Order of Smoothness over Hierarchical T-Meshes
item.description: arXiv:2507.11047v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the dimension of the spline space of di-degree $(d,d)$ with the highest order of smoothness over a hierarchical T-mesh $\mathscr T$ using the smoothing cofactor-conformality method. Firstly, we obtain a dimensional formula for the conformality vector space over a tensor product T-connected component. Then, we prove that the dimension of the conformality vector space over a T-connected component of a hierarchical T-mesh under the tensor product subdivision can be calculated in a recursive manner. Combining these two aspects, we obtain a dimensional formula for the bi-degree $(d,d)$ spline space with the highest order of smoothness over a hierarchical T-mesh $\mathscr T$ with mild assumption. Additionally, we provide a strategy to modify an arbitrary hierarchical T-mesh such that the dimension of the bi-degree $(d,d)$ spline space is stable over the modified hierarchical T-mesh. Finally, we prove that the dimension of the spline space over such a hierarchical T-mesh is the same as that of a lower-degree spline space over its CVR graph. Thus, the proposed solution can pave the way for the subsequent construction of basis functions for spline space over such a hierarchical T-mesh.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Huang B, Chen F. Dimension of bi-degree (d, d) spline spaces with the highest order of smoothness over hierarchical T-meshes. Science China Mathematics, 2026: 1-24
item.dc:creator: Bingru Huang, Falai Chen

item.title: Artifacts of Numerical Integration in Learning Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2507.14491v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In many applications, one needs to learn a dynamical system from its solutions sampled at a finite number of time points. The learning problem is often formulated as an optimization problem over a chosen function class. However, in the optimization procedure, prediction data from generic dynamics requires a numerical integrator to assess the mismatch with the observed data. This paper reveals potentially serious effects of a chosen numerical scheme on the learning outcome. Specifically, the analysis demonstrates that a damped oscillatory system may be incorrectly identified as having "anti-damping" and exhibiting a reversed oscillation direction, even though it adequately fits the given data points. This paper shows that the stability region of the selected integrator will distort the nature of the learned dynamics. Crucially, reducing the step size or raising the order of an explicit integrator does not, in general, remedy this artifact, because higher-order explicit methods have stability regions that extend further into the right half complex plane. Furthermore, it is shown that the implicit midpoint method can preserve either conservative or dissipative properties from discrete data, offering a principled integrator choice even when the only prior knowledge is that the system is autonomous.
item.dc:creator: Bing-Ze Lu, Richard Tsai

item.title: On the optimization of discrepancy measures
item.description: arXiv:2508.04926v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Points in the unit cube with low discrepancy can be constructed using algebra or, more recently, by direct computational optimization of a criterion. The usual $L_\infty$ star discrepancy is a poor criterion for this because it is computationally expensive and lacks differentiability. Its usual replacement, the $L_2$ star discrepancy, is smooth but exhibits other pathologies shown by J. Matou\v{s}ek. In an attempt to address these problems, we introduce the \textit{average squared discrepancy} which averages over $2^d$ versions of the $L_2$ star discrepancy anchored in the different vertices of $[0,1]^d$. Not only can this criterion be computed in $O(dn^2)$ time, like the $L_2$ star discrepancy, but also we show that it is equivalent to a weighted symmetric $L_2$ criterion of Hickernell's by a constant factor. We compare this criterion with a wide range of traditional discrepancy measures, and show that only the average squared discrepancy avoids the problems raised by Matou\v{s}ek. Furthermore, we present a comprehensive numerical study showing in particular that optimizing for the average squared discrepancy leads to strong performance for the $L_2$ star discrepancy, whereas the converse does not hold. This version corrects some of the threshold sample sizes n at which random points become better than n repeated points for some discrepancy measures. In particular, the periodic L_2 discrepancy has no repeated point pathology.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Cl\'ement, Nathan Kirk, Art B. Owen, T. Konstantin Rusch

item.title: Higher Order Unfitted Space-Time Methods for Transport Problems
item.description: arXiv:2509.02253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we present an Unfitted Space-Time Finite Element method for the scalar transport equation posed on moving domains. We consider the case of the domain boundary being transported by the same velocity field as the scalar concentration inside the physical domain. A standard continuous Galerkin Finite element space is considered on a fixed background mesh, as well as tensor product Space-Time elements, which can be discontinuous along time slice boundaries. For the computational geometry, we opt for a spatially second-order accurate approximation variant in the mathematical analysis. In particular, we establish stability in a problem-specific norm and prove a priori error bounds of high order. Numerical examples illustrate these theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Erik Burman, Fabian Heimann

item.title: IGA-LBM: Isogeometric lattice Boltzmann method
item.description: arXiv:2509.11427v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) offers intrinsic parallelism and simple boundary treatment, but Cartesian lattices approximate curved boundaries by stair steps, causing spurious forces and boundary-layer errors. We present an isogeometric collocation lattice Boltzmann method (IGA-LBM) that solves the discrete-velocity BGK system in strong form on body-fitted B-spline and NURBS geometries. Distribution functions are collocated at Greville points, advection is evaluated with high-order operators on the exact spline mapping, and time integration uses a four-stage Runge-Kutta scheme. Exact geometric metrics preserve a uniform free stream to machine precision on curved grids while retaining formal accuracy. The analysis recovers the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with viscosity nu = cs^2 tau and shows that the main isogeometric advantage is exact geometry rather than a new interior stencil. Centered collocation is stabilized by a high-order filter, a physical-node closure restores fourth-order accuracy near clustered walls, and stiff collision limits the explicit step to dt <= 2.785 tau, scaling as O(Re^-1). Tests confirm the predicted accuracy and the O(Ma^2) compressibility floor. Validation covers the Ghia lid-driven cavity, steady and unsteady flow past a circular cylinder, and a body-fitted NACA0012 airfoil. For the cylinder, recirculation length is within about 9 percent and the Strouhal number within about 2.5 percent of reference values; drag is 6-12 percent above consensus and decreases with refinement, with stable wakes up to Re = 1000. For NACA0012 at Re = 500 and 10 degrees incidence, surface pressure and skin friction agree with reference data within a few percent. The method provides a high-order, free-stream-preserving LBM for curved-boundary flows based on exact B-spline and NURBS geometry, with demonstrated accuracy, stability, and geometric fidelity.
item.dc:creator: Ye Ji, Monica L\u{a}c\u{a}tu\c{s}, Matthias M\"oller

item.title: Convergent Compact Finite Difference Methods with Symmetric Matrices and Highest Possible Orders for Variable-Coefficient Elliptic Equations
item.description:

Although 2nd-order compact symmetric FDMs for variable-coefficient Poisson equations are known, the construction of higher-order counterparts has, to the best of our knowledge, remained an open problem. This is largely because all stencils must satisfy highly specific interdependent relations and high-order consistency imposes numerous local technical conditions. This paper provides a comprehensive characterization of the highest consistency order that a $d$-dimensional compact symmetric FDM can achieve for variable-coefficient Poisson equations on a uniform grid. For the 1D case, we prove that our symmetric compact FDMs on a uniform grid can achieve arbitrary consistency orders, yield tridiagonal SPD matrices, and converge at the corresponding orders in the $\infty$-norm and the weighted $2$-norm. For any $d$-dimensional case with $d\ge 2$, we prove that compact (not necessarily symmetric) FDMs can achieve 6th-order consistency and that no higher consistency order is possible. If $	frac{|
