item.dc:creator: Qiwei Feng, Bin Han, Michelle Michelle, Jiwoon Sim

item.title: Multiscale Graph Reduction for Heterogeneous and Anisotropic Discrete Diffusion Processes
item.description: arXiv:2510.10894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present multiscale graph-based reduction algorithms for upscaling heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems. The proposed coarsening approaches begin by constructing a partition of the computational domain into a set of balanced local subdomains, resulting in a standard type of domain decomposition. Given this initial decomposition, general coarsening techniques based on spectral clustering are applied within each subgraph to accurately identify the key microscopic features of a given system. The spectral clustering algorithm is based on local generalized eigen-decompositions applied to the signed graph Laplacian. The resulting coarse-fine splittings are combined with two variants of energy-minimizing strategies for constructing coarse bases for diffusion problems. The first is an unconstrained minimization formulation in which local harmonic extensions are applied column-wise to construct multi-vector preserving interpolation in each region, whereas the second approach is a variant of the constrained energy minimization formulations derived in the context of non-local multi-continua upscaling techniques. We apply the resulting upscaling algorithms to a variety of tests arising from the graph Laplacian, including diffusion in the perforated domain, channelized media, highly anisotropic settings, and discrete pore network models to demonstrate the potential and robustness of the proposed coarsening approaches. We show numerically and theoretically that the proposed approaches lead to accurate coarse-scale models and approximations relative to the corresponding fine-scale discrete system and corresponding approximation. Initial results of a two-level solver applied to these same test problems that uses in addition a block smoother with coloring are also provided.
item.dc:creator: Maria Vasilyeva, James Brannick, Ben S. Southworth

item.title: The $L_p$-error rate for randomized quasi-Monte Carlo self-normalized importance sampling of unbounded integrands
item.description: arXiv:2511.10599v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS) is a fundamental tool in Bayesian inference when the posterior distribution involves an unknown normalizing constant. In many applications, both the test function of interest and the underlying state space are unbounded, making direct $L_1$-error (mean absolute error) and $L_2$-error (root mean square error) estimates challenging for SNIS under randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) sampling. In this work, we derive the $L_p$-error rate $(p\ge1)$ for RQMC-based SNIS (RQMC-SNIS) estimators with unbounded integrands on unbounded domains. A key step in our analysis is to first establish the $L_p$-error rate for plain RQMC integration. Our results allow for a broader class of transport maps used to generate samples from RQMC points. Under mild function boundary growth conditions, we further establish the \(L_p\)-error rate of order \(\mathcal{O}(N^{-\beta + \epsilon})\) for RQMC-SNIS estimators, where $\epsilon>0$ is arbitrarily small, $N$ is the sample size, and \(\beta \in (0,1]\) depends on the boundary growth rate of the resulting integrand. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Du, Zhijian He

item.title: A sixth-order compact time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral method for the Dirac equation
item.description: arXiv:2601.19172v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel sixth-order compact time-splitting scheme, denoted as $ S_{6\text{c}}$, for solving the Dirac equation in the absence of external magnetic potentials. This method is easy to implement, and it provides a substantial reduction in computational complexity compared to the existing sixth-order splitting schemes. By incorporating a time-ordering technique, we also extend $S_{6\text{c}}$ to address problems with time-dependent potentials. Comprehensive comparisons with various time-splitting methods show that $S_{6\text{c}}$ exhibits significant advantages in terms of both precision and efficiency. Moreover, numerical results indicate that $S_{6\text{c}}$ maintains the super-resolution property for the Dirac equation in the nonrelativistic regime in the absence of external magnetic potentials.
item.dc:creator: Weiguo Gao, Zhansi He, Jia Yin

item.title: Advances on the recovery of (perturbed) Cauchy matrices
item.description: arXiv:2602.14609v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a (possibly approximate) Cauchy matrix, how can we efficiently compute its generators? Expanding on previous work by Liesen and Luce [Linear Algebra Appl. 493 (2016) 261--280], we present a general family of algorithms for Cauchy parameter recovery, together with new error estimates. We also introduce a displacement-based approximation, which leads to a new algorithm for Cauchy parameter recovery. Numerical experiments show that the algorithm based on the displacement approximation is generally more accurate than the other algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Paola Boito, Dario Fasino, Beatrice Meini

item.title: FFT-accelerated computation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for inhomogeneous exterior Helmholtz problems using the method of fundamental solutions
item.description: arXiv:2603.15378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An efficient numerical method is proposed for computing the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map associated with the exterior Dirichlet problem for the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation with an inhomogeneous term. The solution in the subdomain exterior to a circular artificial boundary is approximated by the method of fundamental solutions (MFS). When the source and collocation points are equally spaced on concentric circles, the coefficient matrices arising in the discretization become circulant, which enables the efficient evaluation of the discrete DtN map by the fast Fourier transform (FFT). By incorporating the transparent boundary condition (TBC) defined by the DtN map into a finite element formulation, the original exterior problem posed in an unbounded domain is reduced to an equivalent problem in a bounded computational domain, which can then be solved by the finite element method (FEM). Numerical examples show that the proposed MFS-based approach provides a highly accurate approximation of the DtN map, that the FFT-based algorithm enables the efficient computation of the resulting discrete DtN map, and that the FEM incorporating the TBC defined by the DtN map yields accurate solutions for exterior Helmholtz problems posed in unbounded domains with an inhomogeneous term.
item.dc:creator: Takemi Shigeta

item.title: Stancu-Type Generalizations of Neural Network Operators with Perturbed Sampling Nodes
item.description: arXiv:2603.15671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a Stancu-type generalization of multivariate neural network operators (NNOs) by incorporating two parameters that perturb the sampling nodes. The proposed operators extend the existing NNOs by allowing flexibility in the placement of sampling nodes. We establish the well-definedness and boundedness of the operators and prove uniform convergence on compact domains. Furthermore, quantitative error estimates are derived in terms of the modulus of continuity, leading to a convergence rate result. A perturbation theorem is also established, showing how the Stancu-type operators differ from the existing NNOs. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the influence of the Stancu parameters on the approximations and to validate the theoretical results. Finally, an application to ECG signal reconstruction is considered, demonstrating that the proposed operators effectively preserve the essential characteristics of the signal while providing accurate approximations.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Saini

item.title: Finite-Budget Convergence and Chaos-Aware Stopping Criteria for Time-Parallel Methods
item.description: arXiv:2604.00855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-parallel algorithms, such as Parareal, are well understood for linear problems, but their convergence analysis for nonlinear, chaotic systems remains limited. This paper introduces a theoretical framework for analysing time-decomposition methods as local contraction mappings with a finite iteration budget. We derive a finite-budget guarantee linking the initial error, convergence rate, and iteration count through a geometric outer--inner-ball condition. We apply this framework to Parareal, deriving explicit estimates for the convergence factor on nonlinear problems. A frozen-Jacobian expansion separates tableau mismatch from Jacobian drift; actual Runge--Kutta maps admit short-window contraction under uniform neighbourhood hypotheses. First-batch defects estimate the initial error, and sampled actual-map derivatives give practical budget predictions covering all six tested weighted-error crossings; guarantees require uniform bounds. For chaos-aware stopping, we introduce a \emph{proximity function} that weights the interface defects (the jumps between chunks) and bounds weighted trajectory error. Numerical experiments on the logistic, Lorenz-63, and Lorenz-96 systems assess early acceptance. With accurate coarse propagation, the chaotic tests typically take two or three fine batches, and accurate prefixes can extend beyond exact chunks. In an independent Lorenz-63 test with inadequate coarse propagation, Lyapunov stopping reduces energy-estimation error relative to coarse-only at lower modelled cost than standard stopping and meets the prescribed adequacy test. Its gain over the zero-correction first fine batch is not significant, however, and a less costly intermediate-step serial solver meets the accuracy limit. An independent Lorenz-96 test finds no clear energy-error improvement. Statistical fidelity is assessed separately from weighted acceptance.
item.dc:creator: Giancarlo Antonino Antonucci, Raphael Andreas Hauser, Debasmita Samaddar, James Buchanan

item.title: Local error estimates for a finite element method combining linear and nonlinear stabilization for the linear hyperbolic transport equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.21775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the combination of a linear continuous interior penalty type and a non-linear artificial diffusion stabilisation applied to the transport problem, based on continuous Galerkin finite elements in space. This method was recently introduced and analysed for globally smooth solutions in [Burman 2023, SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 45, 1, A96-A122]. We provide a rigorous proof of a localisation principle in terms of weighted stability and a priori error bound results, which follow the widely known $\mathcal{O}(h^{k+1/2})$ scaling in the $L^2(\Omega; t=T)$ norm, where $k$ denotes the polynomial order of the finite element space and $h$ the mesh size. The analysis is semi-discrete in space and assumes sufficient local regularity of the continuous solution on the smooth part of the domain, where the continuous interior penalty stabilisation is active, whilst artificial diffusion operates on the remaining rough parts of the domain. Thereby, the analysis demonstrates that typical numerical errors in the rough part stay localised relative to the convection velocity and do not negatively affect the smooth parts of the solution, if the stabilisation combination is set up accordingly.
item.dc:creator: Erik Burman, Fabian Heimann

item.title: Robust Model-Based Iteration for Passive Gamma Emission Tomography
item.description: arXiv:2604.26745v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Passive Gamma Emission Tomography (PGET) is an International Atomic Energy Agency -approved technique for verifying spent nuclear fuel assemblies prior to geological disposal. Reconstructing the emission and attenuation maps from PGET measurements is a nonlinear ill-posed inverse problem, currently solved with a Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) scheme that requires 10-20 iterations to achieve sufficient accuracy. We propose an accelerated iterative solver that combines the LM algorithm with a Deep Gauss-Newton step, in which a learned operator refines the update proposed by the deterministic algorithm at each iteration. A safeguard condition based on the trust-region model ensures that the accelerated iterates perform no worse than LM and retain convergence to a critical point of the regularized objective. Within this framework we compare three architectures for the learned component: an encoder-decoder-style Convolutional Neural Network, Fourier Neural Operators, and Wavelet Neural Operators. Each is trained on a small set of coarsely simulated 9x9 assemblies. Experiments on simulated and real measurements from Finnish nuclear power plants show that the proposed scheme reaches LM-quality reconstructions in roughly one third of the iterations, while revealing architecture-dependent trade-offs in robustness against out-of-distribution inputs.
item.dc:creator: Tommi Heikkil\"a, Sara Heikkinen, Riina Rimppi, Tapio Helin

item.title: Improving accuracy of finite element solutions by smoothing
item.description: arXiv:2605.04786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a smoothing-based postprocessing method for improving the accuracy of finite element solutions. The method applies a few smoothing iterations, such as damped Jacobi, symmetrized Gauss-Seidel, or preconditioned conjugate gradient, with the initial guess being the current finite element solution embedded in an augmented finite element space. The resulting procedure is algebraic, easy to implement, and applicable to high-order and three-dimensional discretizations. For symmetric and positive-definite problems, we show that the accuracy of the smoothed solutions is improved by a smoothing factor under additive and multiplicative smoothers. This smoothing factor decays exponentially during the first few smoothing steps. The effectiveness of the proposed method is numerically demonstrated using the Poisson, Maxwell, biharmonic and Helmholtz equations.
item.dc:creator: Yuwen Li, Han Shui, Ludmil Zikatanov

item.title: Quantum circuits for the advection-diffusion equation with boundary conditions based on LCHS
item.description: arXiv:2605.17542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a systematic and explicit quantum circuit framework for solving advection-diffusion equations with boundary conditions, based on the Linear Combination of Hamiltonian Simulations (LCHS) method.By employing the Finite Volume Method (FVM) combined with various flux construction schemes, we elaborate the design of quantum circuits tailored explicitly for Robin boundary conditions (including Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions as special cases) and periodic boundary conditions. The Robin boundary elimination is encoded by newly constructed endpoint-projector circuits, and all physical and boundary-induced inhomogeneous terms are incorporated through an outer linear combination of unitaries (LCU). The error analysis adopts an LCU-weighted form, preserving the decay of the LCHS kernel in the product-formula bounds. Complementing this analysis, a comprehensive gate complexity analysis demonstrates the quantum advantages over classical computing in high-dimensional scenarios. We simulate the proposed circuits on a fault-tolerant emulator, and numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework across homogeneous, inhomogeneous, and high-dimensional cases.The proposed framework is compatible with numerous spatial discretization methods and numerical schemes, extends naturally to other linear PDEs, and establishes a practical foundation for solving large-scale PDE problems on future fault-tolerant quantum computers.
item.dc:creator: Leyu Chen, Tiegang Liu, Liang Xu, Kun Wang

item.title: Mixed finite element discretization of intrinsic geometrically exact beams for multiplier-free multibody dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.20245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Reissner-Simo and Hodges models are two equivalent continuous descriptions of finite-strain beam dynamics. The Reissner-Simo formulation uses displacements and rotations, while the Hodges formulation is intrinsic and avoids both variables. Although equivalent in theory, the two approaches behave differently after discretization and offer distinct numerical advantages. In this work, we develop a structure-preserving discretization of the intrinsic planar beam formulation. Because the intrinsic equations involve linear differential operators, both kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions can be imposed naturally using mixed finite elements. The resulting formulation also enables multibody systems to be assembled without algebraic constraints, avoiding the stiff differential-algebraic equations typically introduced by kinematic constraints. We demonstrate the approach on different examples, also showing that closed kinematic loops can be modeled without algebraic constraints. The resulting interconnected systems retain a port-Hamiltonian structure, with all nonlinearities confined to the interconnection operator. This structure allows exact energy preservation when combined with implicit midpoint time integration. Furthermore the scheme appears to require less Newton iterations compared to existing energy preserving scheme.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Brugnoli, Philipp L. Kinon, Francesco Sanfedino, Peter Betsch, Olivier A. Bauchau

item.title: Generalized Modulo Hysteresis Encoding
item.description: arXiv:2608.01270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unlimited sensing and its extension via modulo hysteresis provide an efficient encoding scheme for high dynamic range signals by folding the signal's amplitude into the range of the analog-to-digital converter prior to sampling. Motivated by shortcomings of the modulo hysteresis model, in this work we introduce generalized modulo encoders that flexibly design the folding by incorporating a general transition function and allowing the folding times to depend on the nonideality of the folding transition. We rigorously study mathematical properties of the respective operators and derive conditions under which a bandlimited signal is uniquely determined by its generalized modulo samples. Finally, we propose a recovery algorithm backed by mathematical guarantees and illustrate our theoretical results through numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Beckmann, J\"urgen Jeschke

item.title: ChromOps.jl: High-order simulation and discrete forward sensitivity analysis for chromatography models
item.description: arXiv:2608.06131v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mechanistic chromatography models are valuable for process development, but gradient-based parameter estimation and optimization can be hindered by computational cost and the effort of deriving objective-function gradients. To address this concern, a fully differentiable Julia chromatography solver, ChromOps.jl, is presented that combines high-order spatial discretization with discrete forward sensitivity analysis (DFSA). Two high-order spatial discretizations, finite difference summation-by-parts (FD-SBP) and the discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DG-SEM), are compared on a 6-component ion-exchange chromatography problem with steric mass action kinetics. Both attain their theoretical convergence rates on manufactured problems, while FD-SBP shows favourable work-precision performance for both forward (primal) and dual-valued simulations and is conceptually simpler to implement. DFSA scales as tDFSA approx 1.4(1+Np)tfwd for up to Np = 24 parameters propagated in a single ForwardDiff.jl chunk, i.e. about 1.4 forward solves per additional parameter. Because the primal and dual-valued solves share the same code path, DFSA provides accurate gradients of user-defined objectives without any hand-derived chain-rule code, enabling accessible gradient-based parameter estimation and optimization.
item.dc:creator: Kristian Meyer, Maksym Ratajczyk, Christopher Rackauckas

item.title: From estimate to proof: certified ground-state energy bounds for singular Schr\"odinger operators on $R^3$
item.description: arXiv:2608.25760v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a rigorous computational method that certifies the separator required by Temple's inequality and its Lehmann--Goerisch refinements, and with it unconditional ground-state bounds for $H=-\Delta+V$ on $R^3$ with attractive Coulomb singularities. For H$_2^+$ the method certifies $\lambda_2^{\rm eee}\ge-0.2035$ in place of the analytic $-\tfrac14$, and Temple's inequality with a global trial then gives an enclosure of width below $6.5\times10^{-51}$. For linear H$_3^{2+}$, whose central nucleus defeats the analytic separator, the certified widths are $1.3\times10^{-12}$ and $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at two nuclear separations. Such a separator, a lower bound on the second eigenvalue, is supplied by theory only for special configurations; elsewhere it is estimated and the bound is conditional. Here every hypothesis is verified in interval arithmetic at run time. Three constructions make this possible on an unbounded domain with a potential of unbounded $L^\infty$ norm: a two-sided Neumann/Dirichlet truncation with a computable remainder; a localized Hardy inequality and sharp form bound with explicit constants, restoring coercivity; and a projection stage that certifies lower bounds on the first two eigenvalues, the second serving as separator. On a box, a Lehmann--Goerisch step places $\lambda_1\in[-0.553291,-0.550740]$ for H$_2^+$. The coercivity constant, we show, must bound its own optimum from above. All drivers and certificates are released.
item.dc:creator: Xuefeng Liu

item.title: On a class of supraconvergent Hermite-type methods for advection-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.14545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop and analyze a class of Hermite-type methods for linear advection-diffusion equations in the case of one-dimensional periodic domains. The methods evolve both nodal values and cell averages and are therefore referred to as hybrid-variable (HV) methods. Using Hermite interpolation theory, we construct the HV methods to arbitrary order of accuracy, and prove that the method is supraconvergent in the sense that the spatial order of accuracy can be up to two orders larger than the local truncation error. In the second part, we prove all central HV methods for linear diffusion equations and linear advection-diffusion equations are stable at the semi-discretized level. Next, we prove the convergence of all stable HV schemes and provide error estimate in the discrete $L^2$-norm of the semi-discretized solution, which extends the supraconvergence from a single mode to all sufficiently smooth initial data. The theoretical predictions on the accuracy and stability of the methods are verified by extensive numerical tests.
item.dc:creator: Xianyi Zeng

item.title: Existence of Dynamical Low-Rank Approximation for SDEs with Locally Lipschitz Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2609.20307v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we consider the Dynamical Low Rank Approximation (DLRA) of a high-dimensional system of Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs); DLRA is an effective reduced order model that projects the equations on a time-varying low dimensional subspace following the evolution of the solution. Well posedness results for the resulting DLRA equations have been proved in arXiv:2308.11581 under the assumption of global Lipschitz continuity and linear growth of the drift and the diffusion coefficients. In this work, we extend the existence result to the case of locally Lipschitz coefficient and we prove uniqueness of solutions under the assumption of a mild growth of the Lipschitz constant to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihito Kazashi, Fabio Nobile, Fabio Zoccolan

item.title: Numerical analysis of parabolic equations with Prandtl--Ishlinskii hysteresis of play type
item.description: arXiv:2609.23676v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rigorous error analysis for numerical approximations of parabolic equations with hysteresis remains limited, even for the widely used Prandtl--Ishlinskii model of play type. In this work, we establish an $O(h+\tau)$ error bound for an implicit Euler $P_1$ finite element discretization. The analysis requires neither higher-order temporal regularity nor additional spatial regularity of the hysteresis variables. For the temporal discretization, we exploit a convex subgradient-flow structure in a weighted Hilbert space and estimates of residual monotone terms to obtain first-order convergence. For the spatial discretization, only the diffusive field is restricted to the finite element space, and a constraint-preserving comparison yields an $O(h)$ semidiscrete estimate. The analysis is developed for play-type Prandtl--Ishlinskii operators formulated directly on a spatial Hilbert space, encompassing the canonical pointwise extension as well as more general spatially structured constraints.
item.dc:creator: Shu Xu, Liqun Cao

item.title: An adaptive localized orthogonal decomposition method for Helmholtz problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.24776v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an adaptive localized orthogonal decomposition (ALOD) method for Helmholtz problems with parametrized loads. Under standard resolution, oversampling, and discrete-stability conditions, we establish, to our knowledge, the first wavenumber-robust residual a posteriori error estimate for a Helmholtz LOD discretization. The estimate is two-sided relative to the fine-grid solution and includes a computable bound for the corrector-localization error. In addition, we design a novel family-aware adaptive algorithm using additive Schwarz corrections to construct a shared regional enrichment space for Helmholtz problems with multiple loads. Energy-weighted proper orthogonal decomposition compresses this space. We establish stability and quasi-optimality of the enriched formulation, with bounds independent of the enrichment space. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of ALOD for multiple loads and large wavenumbers.
item.dc:creator: Yuwen Li, Chuxin Que

item.title: Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers
item.description: arXiv:2609.25087v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-order isogeometric discretizations produce a small number of non-physical outlier modes at the top of the discrete spectrum. These modes can pollute the numerical solution in wave propagation and structural dynamics. Most existing remedies modify the spatial discretization through outlier-free bases, mass lumping, subspace projection, and related constructions. We introduce MIISO (Modal Integrators for Isogeometric Stabilization of Outliers), a family of exponential Rosenbrock-Krylov methods of orders two through six that suppress the outliers in the time integrator and leave the spatial discretization unchanged. We construct a non-holomorphic amplification map by blending a Pad\'e approximation that preserves physical oscillatory modes with a Pade approximation that damps high frequencies, with the blend placed at the known spectral location of the outliers. For orders three and higher the damping approximant is repaired so that the method is unconditionally A-stable. Physical modes receive no numerical dissipation and the outliers are driven to zero. The outlier handling and the method steps are fully matrix-free, and the method extends to nonlinear problems. Numerical experiments recover the predicted orders, match spatial outlier removal without changing the discretization, show lower cost than generalized-alpha at matched accuracy and in scaling, and demonstrate the method on nonlinear and three-dimensional problems.
item.dc:creator: Sreeram Shankar

item.title: Sign-switched antithetic coupling in gradient random-walk methods for convection-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.01120v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an antithetic coupling that reduces the computational cost of gradient random-walk methods for one-dimensional convection-diffusion equations. The methods represent the solution's spatial derivative by particles with positive or negative masses, whose cumulative sums reconstruct the solution, and model diffusion by Gaussian displacements. The particles reorder and, for a nonlinear flux, interact. Antithetic sampling negates the displacements of a second simulation, which positively correlates the contributions of particles matched by position when their masses have opposite signs. Our coupling instead gives matched particles of opposite sign identical displacements and retains opposite displacements for equal-sign pairs. We prove that each simulation keeps the distribution of an uncoupled run as the matching changes, so the averaged solution keeps the bias of one simulation. For fixed particle configurations and matching, the coupling minimizes each matched pair's conditional variance contribution after diffusion among all couplings with the same Gaussian marginal distributions. From the same configurations, its variance reduction over antithetic sampling at the final diffusion stage has a closed form for any flux. For the heat equation, a martingale decomposition extends both results to each step's contribution to the terminal variance. In a Burgers' equation test, the coupling meets a tolerance for the spatially integrated mean squared error with 4 simulations, against 34 for antithetic sampling and 65 for independent sampling. In a second test, it meets a common error tolerance in about 40% less time than pairing particles only within each sign.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Abkin, Prabir Daripa

item.title: Residual Minimisation for Transport-Based Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.02499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider an optimal control problem governed by a stationary linear transport equation in two or three spatial dimensions, motivated by photon transport in radiotherapy treatment planning. The control is an inflow boundary source, and the observation operator may track either the angular flux or its angular integral, the latter serving as a simplified dose surrogate. The associated optimality system consists of a transport--adjoint pair with angular dependence, coupled through a boundary optimality condition. We formulate a residual least-squares functional whose minimisers coincide with solutions of the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker system and show that the functional controls the $L^2$ errors in the state and adjoint and the flux-weighted $L^2$ error in the control. This yields a continuum-level a posteriori estimate without recourse to discretisation. An additional unweighted optimality residual certifies the control in the norm of the objective. The estimate holds for every admissible approximation and accounts for the different boundary measures in the control penalty and transport traces, without a positive lower bound on $|\omega\cdot n|$. We then parameterise the state, adjoint and control using neural networks and minimise over a neural network space using appropriate quadrature. The Monte Carlo formulation replaces each residual integral by a weighted sample mean, whose quadrature error enters the a posteriori estimate. We prove convergence under explicit assumptions on approximation, quadrature and optimisation and derive bounds on the total error in terms of approximation, quadrature and optimisation error. Numerical examples in two and three dimensions illustrate the residual--error relation and the flexibility of the residual framework for field- and dose-tracking control problems, including regular manufactured solutions.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Pryer, Nikolaos Rekatsinas

item.title: Optimal Diagonal Preconditioning Beyond Worst-Case Conditioning: Theory and Practice of Omega Scaling
item.description: arXiv:2509.23439v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study optimal diagonal preconditioning using the classical worst-case $\kappa$-condition number and the averaging-based $\omega$-condition number. For the $\kappa$-optimal preconditioning problem, we derive an affine-based pseudoconvex reformulation with three key advantages: all stationary points are global minima, subgradients are inexpensive to compute, and the optimization variable is an $n$-dimensional vector rather than an $n\times n$ matrix as in semidefinite programming (SDP) approaches. We develop a simple and highly efficient subgradient method, with convergence guarantees, for solving this pseudoconvex formulation that is substantially more scalable and accurate than existing SDP-based methods. For the $\omega$-condition number, we provide explicit characterizations of optimal diagonal and block diagonal preconditioners. In particular, we show that several classical preconditioners, including Jacobi and row/column normalization, are $\omega$-optimal, and that matrix balancing schemes monotonically reduce $\omega$ and converge to stationary points of the two-sided problem. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first unified and explicit characterization of optimality conditions for both $\kappa$ and $\omega$-based preconditioning. Our numerical experiments further reveal a striking phenomenon: although $\kappa$-optimal preconditioners achieve stronger reductions in the worst-case condition number, $\omega$-optimal preconditioners are substantially cheaper to compute and yield better performance for iterative methods such as preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) and least squares method (LSQR). Moreover, applying $\omega$-optimal scaling to linear systems that are already $\kappa$-optimally preconditioned leads to further improvements in PCG iterations.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Ghadimi, Woosuk L. Jung, Arnesh Sujanani, David Torregrosa-Bel\'en, Henry Wolkowicz

item.title: Simulating Clifford Circuits with Gaussian Elimination
item.description: arXiv:2511.06127v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum circuits are considered more powerful than classical circuits and require exponential resources to simulate classically. Clifford circuits are a special class of quantum circuits that can be simulated in polynomial time but still show important quantum effects such as entanglement. In this work, we present an algorithm that simulates Clifford circuits by performing Gaussian elimination on a modified adjacency matrix derived from the circuit structure. Our work builds on a ZX-calculus tensor network representation of Clifford circuits that reduces to quantum graph states. We give a concise formula of amplitudes of graph states based on the LDL decomposition of matrices over GF(2), and use it to get efficient algorithms for strong and weak simulation of Clifford circuits using a tree-decomposition-based sparse LDL algorithm. The complexity of our algorithm matches the state of the art for weak graph state simulation and improves the state of the art for strong graph state simulation by taking advantage of Strassen-like fast matrix multiplication. Our algorithm is also efficient when computing many amplitudes or samples of a Clifford circuit. Further, our amplitudes formula provides a new characterization of locally Clifford equivalent graph states as well as an efficient protocol to learn graph states with low-rank adjacency matrices.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Pang, Edgar Solomonik

item.title: Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework
item.description: arXiv:2511.13879v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an algorithm for studying the sum $$ G_N(x,\rho) = \sum_{k=1}^N \left[ \{x+k\rho\} - \frac{1}{2}\right],$$ which is closely related to the discrepancy of the irrational rotation. Computation of $ G_N $ and associated statistics is notoriously difficult due to numerical instability and the failure of sampling to capture the discontinuities. Our algorithm instead fully defines $G_N$ through its discontinuities, which allows computation of $ G_N (x,\rho)$ with errors on the order of $N$ times machine epsilon in $O(N)$ time for practical $N$. The associated probability density function can then be computed in $O(N \log N)$ time. Presented as a tool for experimental mathematics, the algorithm enables reliable plots of the descriptive statistics of $G_N$ over $N$, in particular the length of the support of the $\text{pdf}$ (the discrepancy), revealing extremal behavior related to the arithmetic properties of $\rho$. We also observe a new pattern: when $\rho$ is well approximated by a continued-fraction convergent $\frac{p_n}{q_n}$, the $\text{pdf}$ exhibits a predictable spiked-trapezoidal pattern when $N=kq_n$, eventually degrading at a rate that appears to depend on approximation quality.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Kravitz, H. (2026). Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework. Experimental Mathematics
item.dc:creator: Hannah Kravitz

item.title: Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Reservoir Seepage Equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.03923v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solving reservoir seepage partial differential equations (PDEs) is critical for hydrocarbon development optimization and production forecasting. Conventional numerical solvers suffer from mesh errors and high computational cost. Standard Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are limited by inefficient parameters. They also face weak high-dimensional representation and poor nonlinear fitting ability. We adapt the Discrete Variable (DV)-Circuit Quantum-Classical Physics-Informed Neural Network (QCPINN) to tackle these drawbacks. This work applies the method to four representative reservoir seepage models. The models cover heterogeneous single-phase pressure diffusion. They also include nonlinear Buckley-Leverett two-phase waterflooding. Another case is adsorption-coupled convection-diffusion compositional flow. The last one refers to fully coupled pressure-saturation two-phase flow with exponential permeability heterogeneity. The QCPINN combines classical preprocessing and postprocessing networks with a DV quantum core. It leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to boost high-dimensional feature mapping. Physical constraints are embedded within the framework to guarantee physically consistent solutions. We evaluate three quantum circuit topologies including Cascade, Cross-mesh and Alternate. Numerical tests prove QCPINNs outperform classical PINNs in prediction accuracy, and the circuit topologies show case-specific performance with clear applicable ranges. This work verifies QCPINN's practicability for reservoir engineering. It bridges quantum computing research with oilfield industrial applications.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Rao, Yina Liu, Yuxuan Shen

item.title: A Level Set Method on Particle Flow Maps
item.description: arXiv:2601.09939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate interface tracking is central to numerical simulations involving moving boundaries, including multiphase flows, free-surface dynamics, phase-change problems, and other interface-driven processes in computational mechanics. Although level set methods provide a flexible implicit representation of evolving interfaces, their grid-based advection and reinitialization procedures often introduce numerical diffusion, volume loss, and degradation of thin or highly curved structures. This paper introduces a Particle Flow Map Level Set (PFM-LS) method that addresses these limitations by transporting interface geometry through particle-carried bidirectional flow maps. In contrast to particle level set methods that use particles mainly as corrective markers, PFM-LS uses particles as primary carriers of level-set values, gradients, and Hessians within a narrow band around the interface. The method combines long-range flow-map transport, high-order particle-grid reconstruction, adaptive particle control, and a hybrid particle-grid redistancing scheme to preserve both signed-distance consistency and sub-grid geometric features. Numerical benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including topology-change tests, chamfer and Hausdorff shape-error metrics, and coupling to an incompressible free-surface flow solver, show that PFM-LS achieves strong volume preservation, high shape fidelity, and near fourth-order convergence, outperforming a broad range of existing level set and reference-map-based methods.
item.dc:creator: Jinjin He, Taiyuan Zhang, Zhiqi Li, Junwei Zhou, Duowen Chen, Bo Zhu

item.title: From Consensus-Based Optimization to Evolution Strategies: Proof of Global Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2602.11677v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is a powerful and versatile zero-order multi-particle method designed to provably solve high-dimensional global optimization problems, including those that are genuinely nonconvex or nonsmooth. The method relies on a balance between stochastic exploration and contraction toward a consensus point, which is defined via the Laplace principle as a proxy for the global minimizer. In this paper, we introduce new CBO variants that address practical and theoretical limitations of the original formulation of this novel optimization methodology. First, we propose a model called $\delta$-CBO}, which incorporates nonvanishing diffusion to prevent premature collapse to suboptimal states. We also develop a numerically stable implementation, the Consensus Freezing scheme, that remains robust even for arbitrarily large time steps by freezing the consensus point over time intervals. We connect these models through appropriate asymptotic limits. Furthermore, we derive from the Consensus Freezing scheme by suitable time rescaling and asymptotics a further algorithm, the Consensus Hopping scheme, which can be interpreted as a form of $(1,\lambda)$-Evolution Strategy. For all these schemes, we characterize for the first time the invariant measures and establish global convergence results, including exponential convergence rates.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Fornasier, Hui Huang, Jona Klemenc, Greta Malaspina

item.title: Risk Control of Traffic Flow Through Chance Constraints and Large Deviation Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2604.01321v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a rare chance-constrained optimal control framework for autonomous traffic management, with traffic dynamics governed by stochastic partial differential equations. To efficiently enforce these probabilistic safety specifications, we exploit a large deviation theory (LDT) based approximation method, which converts the original highly non-convex, sampling-heavy stochastic optimization problem into a tractable deterministic nonlinear programming problem. The proposed LDT-based reformulation exhibits superior computational scalability, as its computational cost remains approximately constant regardless of the target violation probability, as opposed to the scaling challenge of traditional sampling-based methods. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is illustrated through numerical experiments on a ring road with stochastic on-ramp inflow, and evaluated with two representative risk measures, namely, maximum traffic density and speed variation. The results show that the proposed method keeps the violation probability close to the target without parameter tuning and is more than ten times faster than a risk-averse baseline.
item.dc:creator: Rui Xu, Shanyin Tong, Xuan Di

item.title: Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.08844v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a rough-path framework for two-parameter rough differential equations on rectangular and simplicial domains, motivated by the signature kernel and Schwinger--Dyson kernel equations. The theory is formulated in spaces of jointly controlled rough paths and is based on a robust two-parameter rough integration framework. In particular, we introduce a notion of rough integration over two-dimensional simplices at low regularity extending previous results in the literature. Within this setting, we show that the signature kernel equation arises naturally as a two-parameter rough differential equation and establish well-posedness and stability. We also extend the Schwinger--Dyson kernel equation, previously formulated for bounded-variation paths, to rough driving signals, proving existence and uniqueness in appropriate controlled rough path spaces. In the smooth rough path regime, we relate the resulting equations to PDE and integro-differential formulations. Finally, we derive and analyse a numerical scheme for the rough Schwinger--Dyson equation, including runtime and memory complexity estimates, and illustrate its performance with numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Cass, Dan Crisan, Andrea Iannucci, William F. Turner

item.title: On the Robustness of Sparse Randomized Sketching to FP16 Rounding on GPUs
item.description: arXiv:2606.20195v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Randomized sketching replaces large matrices with smaller surrogates that preserve geometry for downstream numerical linear algebra. Sparse sketches promise faster formation than dense projections, but irregular GPU atomic updates become costly when each input row contributes to several output rows, as in SparseStack. FP16 accumulation halves sketch storage and update traffic, relieving cache pressure. How much does this rounding affect sketch geometry and downstream accuracy? For SparseStack with four nonzeros per column, cuSPARSE's FP16 path is slower than its FP32 baseline. Our custom kernel instead pairs FP32 inputs and signed products with packed FP16 vector atomic accumulation, turning lower precision into substantial gains. On NVIDIA H200, it forms complete sketches up to $1.91\times$ faster than our FP32 baseline and up to $1.58\times$ faster than cuSPARSE FP32. Under stated independence and range assumptions, random sketch signs cancel round-to-nearest conversion-error cross terms, giving expected squared Frobenius error no greater than ideal stochastic rounding. We assess accumulation empirically. At a sketch dimension of twice the number of input columns, the least-squares pipeline is $1.44$-$1.47\times$ faster than FP32, with median paired residual increases below $0.4\%$. Rescaling exposes range limitations and cases where stochastic conversion degrades accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Aryaman Jeendgar, Cl\'ement Flint, Hartwig Anzt

item.title: Preconditioning Magnetic Systems in Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.26693v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The convergence of the self-consistent field iterations in Kohn-Sham density functional theory can be significantly hindered by the presence of small eigenvalues in the dielectric matrix, which are often associated with electronic phase transitions in magnetic systems. In this work, we study this type of convergence issues and propose a new preconditioning scheme to mitigate them. Our preconditioning scheme is inspired by the Stoner model and based on a non-interacting susceptibility that neglects orbital variations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of ferromagnetic systems, showing that it can significantly reduce the number of iterations required to achieve convergence in the vicinity of magnetic phase transitions.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ementine Barat, Antoine Levitt, Marc Torrent

item.title: Error-Conditioned Neural Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2606.27354v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural surrogate models offer fast approximate mappings from PDE parameters to solutions, but they typically treat solving as a purely statistical task: once trained, they struggle to correct their own constraint violations and extrapolate beyond the training distribution. Recent hybrid methods promote physical correctness by targeting the PDE residual via gradient descent or Gauss--Newton steps, but inherit the compute cost and instability of the underlying classical optimizers. We show, theoretically and empirically, that numerically minimizing the PDE residual can be an unreliable proxy for reconstruction accuracy in ill-conditioned systems, explaining why these methods often do not make accurate predictions despite achieving low residuals. We propose error-conditioned Neural Solvers (ENS), built on a different principle: rather than an optimization target, the PDE residual field is passed as a direct input to the network at each iteration, enabling it to read the spatial structure of its own errors and learn an update policy to iteratively correct its predictions. Across four PDE families, ENS attains the highest prediction accuracy in the large majority of settings, with gains reaching $10\times$ on turbulent Kolmogorov flow, while avoiding the expensive compute cost of hybrid methods. ENS's learned correction policy generalizes under distribution shift, including zero-shot parameter changes and cross-equation transfer, where its relative advantage is largest in the ill-conditioned regimes where residual minimization is least reliable. Project website: https://neuralsolver.github.io/.
item.dc:creator: Haina Jiang, Liam Wang, Peng-Chen Chen, Min Seop Kwak, Seungryong Kim, Brian Bell, Jeong Joon Park

item.title: A neural delta-$f$ particle-in-cell method: evolving the background with learned backward flows
item.description: arXiv:2606.30622v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a novel {\delta}f particle-in-cell (PIC) method for the kinetic simulation of electrostatic plasmas in which the bulk density, acting as a control variate, is evolved using symplectic neural networks (SympNets). The SympNets are used as an approximation of the backward flow and trained using the particle trajectories. We introduce a periodic variant of the SympNet architecture that encodes the spatial periodicity of the problem into the network itself. We validate the approach with numerical results in 1D1V and 3D3V for the Vlasov-Poisson system.

item.title: A Spectral-Domain Pseudo-Inverse Method for True 3D Gravity Inversion
item.description: arXiv:2608.11014v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main difficulty in 3D gravity inversion is that surface observations lack vertical wavenumber information, making the problem underdetermined and depth resolution poor. Building on the author's spectral-domain pseudo-inverse theory for unitary diagonalizable systems, this paper presents a true 3D inversion method. Surface data are analytically continued upward via Laplace's equation to form a 3D data volume, providing the vertical wavenumber sampling for the 3D Fourier transform. A general analytical expression for the half-space spectrum is derived, separating the horizontal spectrum from the vertical propagation kernel. The Green's function of the 3D Poisson equation is unitarily diagonalized, yielding the forward spectral response $\lambda(\kk) = -i 4\pi G k_z / K^2$, and a stable inverse filter $q_\alpha(\lambda) = \bar{\lambda}/(|\lambda|^2 + \alpha)$ is constructed. This filter is proved to have bounded stability and consistency (reducing to the exact inverse as $\alpha \to 0^+$). Validation with a homogeneous sphere model shows correct recovery of the anomaly location and singular behavior at the source. The contributions are twofold: (1) upward continuation constructs a 3D volume from 2D surface data, which does not add physical observations but unfolds the 3D spatial variation information (data innovation) derived through the governing physical equation; (2) the inversion is reduced to one forward 3D Fourier transform, one spectral scaling, and one inverse transform. The framework extends to any linear potential-field inverse problem with a translation-invariant forward operator, including magnetic inversion.

item.title: Fully discrete stochastic maximal regularity and $H^\infty$-calculus for second-order elliptic operators
item.description:
arXiv:2609.07436v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes the fully discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-regularity and the accompanying sharp maximal estimate for numerical approximations of parabolic stochastic partial differential equations. We consider the spatial finite element discretization $A_h$ of a general second-order elliptic operator $A=-
abla \cdot a
abla +b\cdot 
abla +c$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a smooth, bounded, convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, coupled with a broad class of temporal schemes, including rational approximations and the exponential Euler method. To obtain these optimal discrete regularity results, we establish a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the discrete spatial operator $A_h$, uniformly in the mesh size $h$. As a direct byproduct, we also establish the discrete-in-space stochastic maximal regularity for the corresponding spatial semi-discretizations. As an application, we establish the pathwise uniform convergence of a fully discrete approximation of the three-dimensional stochastic Allen--Cahn equation with variable diffusion coefficients and multiplicative noise.
item.dc:creator: Foivos Evangelopoulos-Ntemiris

item.title: A Geometrically Parameterized Quasi-Stationary 3D Model for High-Frequency Induction Tube Welding
item.description: arXiv:2609.11250v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A three-dimensional multiphysics finite element model for the simulation of high-frequency induction welding of tubes is presented. The model couples a time-harmonic $h-\phi$ formulation with a stabilized quasi-stationary advection-diffusion heat transport equation, enabling accurate prediction of electromagnetic and thermal fields under industrial operating conditions. The model incorporates parameterized geometry generation and semi-automated, physics-tailored mesh construction and is implemented using the open-source tools GetDP and Gmsh. Validation against measurements from a commercial induction welding line for AISI 304 stainless steel tubes demonstrates good agreement with operating data. The validated model is subsequently applied to investigate the influence of impeder material by comparing a conventional FeNiZnV ferrite with the soft magnetic composite Ferrotron 559H for the induction welding of AISI 304 stainless steel tubes.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Ivanov, John Inge Asperheim, Bj{\o}rnar Grande, Prerana Das

item.title: Higher-Order Approximation of Exit Functionals in Sampling-Based Stochastic Model Predictive Control
item.description: arXiv:2609.25257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Safety evaluation in sampling-based stochastic model predictive control often requires numerical estimation of exit functionals. The approximation of first-exit times and exit indicators is therefore a key numerical bottleneck, and discretization error in these quantities directly affects the resulting controller. This paper studies how existing higher-order methods for strong approximation of exit times can be brought into safe control. Two cases are highlighted. For general noncommutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1 Milstein discretization is used together with L\'evy-area simulation via Wiktorsson's method. For commutative dynamics, an adaptive order-1.5 construction achieves a stronger exit-time rate. Under a local anti-concentration condition on the exit-time law, we show that strong exit-time approximation transfers to strong approximation of the failure indicator. The methods are then studied in the context of chance-constrained path integral control, which provides an exact continuous-time representation of safety through exit events. Numerical experiments compare the two cases in terms of strong exit-time error, failure-indicator error, and closed-loop constraint satisfaction, showing improvement over Euler-Maruyama and thereby enabling existing and future techniques whose applicability depends on improved strong approximation.
item.dc:creator: Sashank Modali, Takashi Tanaka
